world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Only comparative wordlist data (Smith 2017 Borneo thesis); no phonological description of Jangkang located

new_statements.quote: From a historical point of view, the existence of a full/reduced vowel distinction in the penultimate syllable is unexpected for two reasons: 1) the modern Land Dayak languages are stress-final, a pattern which is likely reconstructable to the proto-language. It is typologically unexpected for unstressed vowels to have a greater number of distinctions than stressed vowels. [fn. 2, p. 112:] Southern Land Dayak includes Golik, Kembayan, Jangkang, Ribun, and Sanggau, among others.
new_statements.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2019. A second look at Proto-Land Dayak vowels. Oceanic Linguistics 58(1): 110-142.
new_statements.locator: p. 111 (sec. 1, first paragraph after Table 2); fn. 2 p. 112 for Jangkang's membership in Southern Land Dayak

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the final syllable of the word in all modern Land Dayak languages, a group that includes Jangkang (Southern Land Dayak). Corroborated at family level by Smith 2017 p. 185 ('stress in many of the languages of West Kalimantan is consistently word-final, a feature of most of the Land Dayak languages of the Kapuas River area') and Rensch et al. 2012 p. 293 ('[the contemporary Land Dayak languages] consistently accent the final syllable of the stem; this is especially evident in utterance-final position'). No source states the rule for Jangkang by name.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated for Jangkang. Rensch et al. 2012 p. 293 add that final accent is 'especially evident in utterance-final position'; Smith 2017 p. 152 and Smith 2019 discuss reduced/merged penultimate vowels (Jangkang penult *a/*ə > o) consistent with unstressed penults.
new_statements.domain_note: Family-level generalization (Land Dayak / Southern Land Dayak), not a Jangkang-specific description; word-level stress; Rensch et al. restrict the Bidayuh statement to citation forms and stems. Smith's Land Dayak data include his own Jangkang wordlist (Semirau village), so the generalization presumably covers his Jangkang data, but no Jangkang phonology has been published.
new_statements.identity_note: Jangkang (Glottolog jang1257, ISO djo; ISO name 'Djongkang' until 2008). Speakers call the language Bekidoh/Bokidoh (Untan articles). Ethnologue/id.wikipedia dialects: Jangkang proper and Pompang. The quoted statements are about Land Dayak as a whole (Smith 2019, Rensch et al. 2012) or the Land Dayak languages of the Kapuas area (Smith 2017); Jangkang is placed in Southern Land Dayak with Ribun (ribu1245), Golik, Sanggau (sang1339) and Kembayan (kemb1250). Smith's Land Dayak data include his own Jangkang wordlist from Semirau village.

sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Jangkang data are Smith's own (Semirau, consultants Linis and Amel). Land Dayak sec. 2.6 pp. 139-168 is historical phonology with Jangkang reflexes (Table 53 p. 152, *-ih > -is pp. 156-157) but no synchronic stress remark for Jangkang. p. 185 (sec. 2.8.2): 'stress in many of the languages of West Kalimantan is consistently word-final, a feature of most of the Land Dayak languages of the Kapuas River area.'

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R., Carolyn M. Rensch, Jonas Noeb & Robert Sulis Ridu. 2012. The Bidayuh Language: Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow (revised and expanded). SIL e-Book 33. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: p. 293 (6.2.4): 'an accentual difference is not evident in the contemporary Land Dayak languages. They consistently accent the final syllable of the stem; this is especially evident in utterance-final position.' Sarawak Bidayuh focus (p. 48: ultima receives peak of word stress in citation forms). Appendix IV p. 424 lists two Pusat Bahasa wordlists from Jangkang district (Semirau: Dayak Tebuas; Tanggung: Dayak Jongkang), wordlists only. Nothing Jangkang-specific on stress.
References: Smith 2017: 139-168, Smith & Rama 2022, Ethnologue 2025 only; no descriptive work listed.
